articles.body: In 1952, a Mickey Mantle baseball card could be bought as part of a wax-wrapped packet for only a penny or a nickel. Seventy years later, one of those cards sold for $12.6 million at auction, setting a new record for sports memorabilia. The 1952 Topps card had already attracted collectors before the record sale. In 1991, Anthony Giordano bought one for $50,000 at a baseball card show at Madison Square Garden. According to The New York Times, the card was eventually graded Mint+ 9.5 out of 10, with its condition described as exceptional. Its value then rose far beyond its original price.1952 Baseball card becomes most expensive ever soldThe 2022 auction marked a major milestone for the card. The $12.6 million result made it the first sports item to sell at auction for eight figures. It also surpassed the previous record of $9.3 million, which had been set earlier in 2022 by the jersey worn by Diego Maradona when he scored the goal known as the “Hand of God” during the 1986 World Cup.Chris Ivy said, “We always knew this card would shatter records and expectations,” while adding that the achievement remained a thrill. The sale also came as the sports collectable market was experiencing strong growth, particularly since the beginning of the coronavirus pandemic in 2020. The article noted that baseball cards can carry a sense of nostalgia, while collectors and others had increasingly begun viewing them as valuable assets.Mickey Mantle card preserved for 70 yearsThe card's condition was a major part of its appeal. Heritage Auctions said Sportscard Guaranty Corporation had graded it “Mint+ 9.5” out of 10. The grading organisation authenticates and grades trading cards, and Ivy described the card as almost perfectly centred, with four sharp corners and beautiful colour.Ivy also highlighted the extraordinary preservation of the card, saying, “The fact that it remained in this condition for 70 years, before being graded, is truly a miracle.” The combination of its condition and its subject, Mickey Mantle, helped distinguish the card when it eventually came to auction.Who owned the 1952 baseball cardBefore reaching its $12.6 million auction price, the card had been owned by Anthony Giordano, the president of a recycling and solid waste business in New Jersey. According to Heritage Auctions, the buyer was an anonymous baseball fan from Rye, New York. Giordano said he had bought the card in 1991 while attending a Father's Day baseball card show at Madison Square Garden with his son.Giordano paid $50,000 for the card in 1991, which was then a record price for that particular card. He and his son had been searching for a 1952 Mantle card, but had not found one they wanted until then. Recalling the purchase, Giordano said, “When we saw the price on this card, we knew it had to be something special.” More than three decades later, that $50,000 purchase was part of a $12.6 million auction sale.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body:
India have been a cut above everyone else in this Women's Asia Cup, and they head into Thursday's semi-final against Bangladesh at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium as heavy favourites.

A perfect record through the group stage, dominant performances with bat and ball, and an opening partnership that no team has been able to contain; everything points to India being right where they want to be.

The batting hasn't even been properly tested yet, which speaks volumes about how comfortably India have gone about their business.

Smriti Mandhana is in the form of her life. She smashed a record-breaking century against Hong Kong in the group stage, and she'll be the danger woman again on Thursday. Opening partner Shafali Verma is equally dangerous as she's scored 543 runs in 19 T20I innings in 2026 at a strike rate of 151.67, with five fifties along the way.

Bangladesh got here through a 34-run win over the UAE in their final Group B fixture, which sealed their semi-final place. Nigar Sultana's team are unlikely to make many changes after that win, with Rabeya Khan and Sharmin Akter both expected to retain their places in the XI.

India vs. Bangaldesh Women's Asian Cup 2026: Toss result, score & live updates

A thoroughly one-sided masterclass wrapped up unusually! Nandani Sharma strikes again as Rabeya Khan loses her balance attempting a sweep against a slower ball, only for her wayward bat to roll onto the stumps. A clinical finish to send India through to the grand finale.

A relentless procession of wickets has derailed Bangladesh's chase. The past five overs have seen them muster just 33 runs while surrendering three crucial wickets. Pratika Rawat delivered the knockout punch by removing skipper Nigar Sultana, while Deepti Sharma ran through Sobhana Mostary and Sharmin Akhter. With the asking rate spiralling past 20 an over, India are cruising toward an emphatic, one-sided victory in Dubai.

Despite a couple of lapses in the field with two dropped catches, India's bowling unit has maintained relentless discipline. Shrewd bowling changes have kept Bangladesh guessing, completely drying up easy scoring avenues. As Nigar Sultana and Sobhana Mostary struggle for fluency and the asking rate breaches the ten-an-over barrier, Bangladesh find themselves pinned against the wall.

Bangladesh made a measured start before Shree Charani broke through to terminate the opening stand. With the required rate climbing, Juairiya Ferdous was coerced into forcing the issue, but misjudged a ball spinning away from her off-stump.

Her attempt to hit across the line resulted in a skier, allowing keeper Richa Ghosh to call loudly and safely pouch the opportunity.

Harmanpreet stayed until the end but struggled to get going as she finished on 24 from 28 balls. However, Deepti Sharma played a cameo of 13 runs from six balls to steer India to 149. A commanding total, and Bangladesh have their work cut out.

India fought their way to 107 for 3 after 16 overs on the back of an emphatic middle-overs turnaround. Shafali Verma led the countercharge with a blistering 40-ball 64 to drag India out of trouble. The finishing duties now rest with Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh to haul the innings past the 150 mark.

India reached 59 for 2 at the halfway stage as Bangladesh successfully squeezed the scoring rate. Having prised out Pratika Rawat, the bowling side holds the upper hand, leaving the onus on Shafali Verma to construct a defining innings if India are to post a competitive total.

India stand at 45/1 after 6 overs. Bangladesh struck early to remove Smriti Mandhana, but an assured stand between Shafali Verma and Pratika Rawal has put India in a commanding position to target 150-plus.
